Analyze only supplied material, not general outside knowledge. Do not invent unreadable content, repair missing diagrams, guess obscured labels or claim to understand audio from video. If a source unit has no excerpts or you interpret native PDF/image/video visual content, use {sourceId,mode:"visual",quote:""}; visual descriptions are interpretations, never verified source facts. Video visual evidence may add time in seconds within its actual duration. Do not fabricate excerpt IDs, repair quotations, or claim a visual reference verifies extracted text. Return exactly {introduction,sections,practice,limitations}. Sections: 1-100 objects with exactly {id,title,kind,paragraphs,steps,evidence}. Choose useful source-anchored sections, not a generic summary. Include a source reference for EVERY supplied source unit somewhere in sections; group related pages if useful. Do not claim that a reference proves a visual interpretation. Each paragraphs array has 1-4 complete plain strings <=1600 characters; steps has 0-6 strings <=800. IDs <=50, title <=140, introduction <=1200, limitations 0-8 strings <=500. Practice MUST be [] for this slice; learners can continue through the source and adapted sections without a generated assessment.
Four supported presentation needs: plain-language (simplify wording, retain source terminology and meaning); stepwise (break the existing source explanation into connected steps, not new worked solutions); visual-description (describe directly visible labels, layout and clearly visible connections only; never infer or invent relationships, arrow directions, signs or multiplicities; explicitly acknowledge ambiguous details); listen (complete, natural spoken statements, no audio autoplay). Combine selected needs where appropriate. Keep keyboard and screen-reader interaction simple for everyone.
For read-spoken, turn spoken source content into readable topic sections with concise key points in steps, preserving supplied details rather than a shallow summary. Unless the learner also requests simplified wording, use the complete supplied sourceUnits.text as the paragraph source, not stitched evidence fragments. Preserve EVERY occurrence of repeated content; never deduplicate, shorten, correct or skip it. Reflow into readable paragraphs only. Check that all paragraphs in order equal the complete transcript ignoring only whitespace. Preserve complete transcript sentences verbatim and use exact continuous source excerpts for key points. Do not join or paraphrase excerpts within a key point. The server verifies all transcript wording is retained in order and each key point is an exact source excerpt. Preserve original order and qualifiers such as may, contributed to, and little regard. When source-preserving output is requested, do not paraphrase facts, strengthen causality, add intentions or introduce explanatory claims. Use neutral source-anchored headings. For read-spoken, make the introduction presentation-only, such as Read the lecture in structured text at your own pace. Do not restate source facts, periods, dates or numbers in the introduction. Never add numeric step labels or reformat dates. The timestamped machine transcript is ASR output, not verified original speech. Never infer inaudible words, non-speech sounds, speaker identities or visual information referenced but absent from the transcript. For audio use text evidence from supplied transcript excerpts only; never visual evidence. Original source code, equations and numbers are displayed beside your explanation. Do not regenerate or modify source code, equations or calculations; refer to the original for exact expressions. Do not introduce new numbers, substitute values, calculate extra answers or create new examples. If you mention a source number, copy its exact written form from the supplied text. Preserve source inconsistencies without silently repairing them. Do not output code blocks, HTML, Markdown, executable content or facts from outside the supplied material. For visual-only content, don't guess unreadable details or use plausible domain knowledge to complete the image. If a requested description cannot be supported, say so in that section and limitations. Do not claim to hear video audio. Use only the provided sourceExcerpts references for extracted-text evidence; otherwise use a visual reference with empty quote.

{"sourceUnits":[{"id":"p1","locator":{"kind":"pdf","page":1}},{"id":"p2","locator":{"kind":"pdf","page":2}},{"id":"p3","locator":{"kind":"pdf","page":3}},{"id":"p4","locator":{"kind":"pdf","page":4}},{"id":"p5","locator":{"kind":"pdf","page":5}},{"id":"p6","locator":{"kind":"pdf","page":6}},{"id":"p7","locator":{"kind":"pdf","page":7}}],"sourceExcerpts":[{"id":"excerpt-1-1","sourceId":"p1","start":0,"end":540,"text":"Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) • Page 1

Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs)

A 7-page mathematics study guide with 8 worked examples.

Learning objectives

• Understand what an ordinary differential equation is.

• Identify order and degree and distinguish linear from nonlinear equations.

• Solve basic first-order ODEs using separation of variables and integrating factors.

• Recognize and solve simple second-order linear homogeneous equations.

• Interpret initial conditions and apply them to obtain particular solutions."},{"id":"excerpt-2-1","sourceId":"p2","start":0,"end":1158,"text":"Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) • Page 2

1. Introduction to ODEs

An ordinary differential equation is an equation involving an unknown function of one independent variable and one or more of its derivatives. ODEs are used to describe quantities that change with respect to another variable, such as time, distance or position.

Basic terminology

• The order of an ODE is the highest derivative appearing in the equation.

• The degree is the power of the highest-order derivative after the equation has been made polynomial in its

derivatives.

• An ODE is linear if the dependent variable and its derivatives occur only to the first power and are not

multiplied together.

• A solution is a function that satisfies the differential equation on an appropriate interval.

Example 1 — Identify order and degree

• Consider: y''' + 4y'' - y' + 7y = 0.

• The highest derivative is y''', so the order is 3. The highest derivative occurs to the first power, so the

degree is 1.

Example 2 — Classify an ODE

• Consider: y' + 3y = x².

• This is a first-order linear ODE because y and y' occur only to the first power and are not multiplied

together."},{"id":"excerpt-3-1","sourceId":"p3","start":0,"end":743,"text":"Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) • Page 3

2. First-Order ODEs: Separation of Variables

A separable differential equation can be rearranged so that all terms involving the dependent variable are on one side and all terms involving the independent variable are on the other.

General pattern

• If dy/dx = f(x)g(y), rearrange to dy/g(y) = f(x) dx, then integrate both sides.

Example 3 — Separable equation

• Solve dy/dx = 3x²y.

• Separate: dy/y = 3x² dx.

• Integrate: ln|y| = x³ + C.

• Therefore: y = Ce^(x³).

Example 4 — Separable equation with an initial condition

• Solve dy/dx = 2xy, given y(0) = 5.

• Separate: dy/y = 2x dx.

• Integrate: ln|y| = x² + C, so y = Ce^(x²).

• Using y(0)=5 gives C=5.

• Therefore: y = 5e^(x²)."},{"id":"excerpt-4-1","sourceId":"p4","start":0,"end":618,"text":"Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) • Page 4

3. First-Order Linear ODEs

A first-order linear ODE can be written in the standard form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x). It is commonly solved using an integrating factor.

Integrating factor

• The integrating factor is μ(x) = e^(∫P(x)dx). Multiplying the equation by μ converts the left-hand side into the

derivative of μy.

Example 5 — Integrating factor method

• Solve dy/dx + 2y = 4.

• Here P(x)=2, so μ=e^(∫2dx)=e^(2x).

• Multiply through: e^(2x)y' + 2e^(2x)y = 4e^(2x).

• Thus d/dx(e^(2x)y)=4e^(2x).

• Integrating gives e^(2x)y=2e^(2x)+C.

• Therefore: y=2+Ce^(-2x)."},{"id":"excerpt-5-1","sourceId":"p5","start":0,"end":676,"text":"Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) • Page 5

4. Applications and Initial-Value Problems

An initial-value problem gives a differential equation together with a condition such as y(xn)=yn. The condition determines the arbitrary constant in the general solution.

Example 6 — Initial-value problem

• Solve y' = 6x - 4, given y(1)=3.

• Integrate: y = 3x² - 4x + C.

• Apply y(1)=3: 3 - 4 + C = 3, so C=4.

• Therefore: y = 3x² - 4x + 4.

Common interpretation

• An ODE may describe a rate of change. For example, if y represents the amount of a quantity at time t,

then dy/dt represents its instantaneous rate of change. An initial condition specifies the starting state."},{"id":"excerpt-6-1","sourceId":"p6","start":0,"end":686,"text":"Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) • Page 6

5. Second-Order Linear ODEs

A common second-order linear homogeneous ODE has the form ay'' + by' + cy = 0, where a, b and c are constants. We use the characteristic equation to determine the form of the solution.

Characteristic equation

• Assume y=e^(rx). Substitution gives the characteristic equation ar²+br+c=0.

• If the roots are distinct real numbers rn and rn, then y=Cne^(rnx)+Cne^(rnx).

• If there is a repeated root r, then y=(Cn+Cnx)e^(rx).

Example 7 — Distinct roots

• Solve y'' - 5y' + 6y = 0.

• Characteristic equation: r² - 5r + 6 = 0.

• Factor: (r-2)(r-3)=0, giving r=2 and r=3.

• Therefore: y=Cne^(2x)+Cne^(3x)."},{"id":"excerpt-7-1","sourceId":"p7","start":0,"end":979,"text":"Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) • Page 7

6. Repeated Roots, Summary and Practice

Repeated roots require a second independent solution containing x. This is one of the important cases in second-order linear ODEs.

Example 8 — Repeated root

• Solve y'' - 4y' + 4y = 0.

• Characteristic equation: r² - 4r + 4 = 0 = (r-2)².

• The repeated root is r=2.

• Therefore: y=(Cn+Cnx)e^(2x).

Quick revision checklist

• Can you identify the order and degree of an ODE?

• Can you recognize a separable equation?

• Can you find an integrating factor for a first-order linear equation?

• Can you apply an initial condition to find an arbitrary constant?

• Can you form and solve a characteristic equation for a second-order homogeneous ODE?

Key formulas

• Separable: dy/g(y) = f(x)dx.

• Linear first order: y' + P(x)y = Q(x), with μ=e^(∫P(x)dx).

• Second-order constant coefficients: ar²+br+c=0.

• Distinct roots: y=Cne^(rnx)+Cne^(rnx).

• Repeated root: y=(Cn+Cnx)e^(rx)."}],"limitations":["Visual and mathematical explanations are AI interpretations of the original pages, not verified reconstructions. Unclear details must remain uncertain."],"inputKind":"pdf"}
